newsitem.title: USA: CSCE raises margins on July "C" coffee futures.
newsitem.headline: CSCE raises margins on July "C" coffee futures.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said it raised the margins on the July 1997 coffee "C" contract by $1,000 to $6,000, including a $2,000 spot charge, effective May 6.
The previous margin required for July 1997 was $5,000, which included a $1,000 spot charge.
The margins on the spot May contract, however, were unchanged at $7,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, the exchange said in a statement.
Margins on all other contracts remained at $4,000, the CSCE added.

In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions required a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are CSCE members or members of the trade. However, the $3,000 spot charge for May 1997 and the $2,000 spot charge for July 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these month, the exchange said.
For customers who are not exchange members or a member of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, the CSCE said.
